title: Metrics
body: We need to know how people are using the product in order to improve it. But we need all the analytics to be fully anonymous and untraceable. Any ideas?
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
Ya, that's a good idea to have analytics (anonymous & untraceable). We can indeed record events such as org creation/joining anonymously.

We have;
1 . NeutrinoMetrics looking good but it is in an early stage. (https://neutrinometrics.net/)
2. Evergreen Google Analytics https://www.npmjs.com/package/electron-google-analytics

Let's discuss events types which are better for analytics.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
I love Apple's approach to analytics.

I don't know if there is any detailed documentation, but they have
completely anonymous analytics.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body:
Found some interesting info on Piwik's website:  

https://piwik.pro/gdpr-compliance/  

Also, bundling Tor with the application is an "easy" way to anonymize metadata "out of the box". This is what apps like Ricochet and OnionShare do to anonymize user metadata (including - especially - user IP addresses).

comments.author: Participant 5
comments.body:
As a stop gap to fully anonymous and untraceable metrics, we could also have a dialog asking a user if they'd like to provide metrics to us.

We've talked about adding [`Sentry`](https://sentry.io/welcome/) in before, and another option that includes web3 snooping (though this sounds quite scary) is [`moesif`](https://www.moesif.com/docs/client-integration/browser-js/).

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: This one is important. @lkngtn can you provide 2-3 important metrics that would help us understand how people use the client? With that, I can do some initial research on solutions

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
So we mainly need:
- A way to contact our most active users (they can provide an email via HelpScout, notifications or an opt-in modal)
- A way to know the referrers (where our users come from)

Matomo can totally work for this.

comments.author: Participant 6
comments.body:
Would also add:
- geographic/region data will also be useful for prioritizing localization and other efforts which might be tied to traction in specific regions.

comments.author: Participant 5
comments.body: I'd add that it'd be useful to know which orgs are being visited, and when, which is easily provided via the URL path.

comments.author: Participant 5
comments.body: Closing; we may work on adding analytics in the future but its current effort is deprioritized.
